dataSheet.description: A racing kart with driver: about 160 kg all up, 1.05 m wheelbase, no suspension beyond frame and tire compliance, solid rear axle. The four-wheel model represents the frame and tire flex as a very stiff corner spring.
sources: Class-typical figures from kart homologation sheets (wheelbase 1040–1060 mm, track 1.2–1.4 m, dry mass with driver 155–175 kg, 125 cc engines of 20–30 kW).
Tire feel parameters tuned to a ~1.4 g skidpad on slick kart tires.

Drivetrain [ILLUSTRATIVE]: a 125 cc two-stroke (peak 17 N·m, 18 kW at 11000 rpm) through a centrifugal clutch that engages between 1800 and 4300 rpm and an 11:80 chain reduction (7.3:1) to a solid rear axle, as on a rental or junior kart.

Steering geometry [ILLUSTRATIVE]: kart spindles with large caster and kingpin inclination jack the frame with steer; the linearised jacking rate of 10 mm per radian unloads the inner rear wheel by about a quarter in a steady corner. No assist; direct steering with a short arm.
The driver sits high on a kart, so the drag acts well above the centre of mass; no measurable lift.
dataSheet.notes: Not a specific chassis. The rear is a solid axle (suspension.kind "solid", ADR-0016) driven through a locked differential: both rear wheels turn at one speed and stay upright to the track. On the four-wheel model it pushes at low speed because the inner rear wheel carries load until the steering-geometry jacking (ADR-0012) and lateral transfer unload it, so the fitted skidpad gradient is slightly negative; the per-point steer angles in the golden file show the push easing with speed.
